clue.text: Shrub of that kind could conceal mum

indicators.note: something that conceals another holds it inside, so the first word's letters wrap round the second's

parts.note: 'such' means of that kind
MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A bush of a particular sort might be big enough for a mother to hide behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumach is a variant spelling of sumac, a genus of shrubs and small trees.

clue.text: Tree getting cold, problem in swamp

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other, so its letters go inside

parts.note: to swamp is to drench, to soak
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A tree in a marsh has a problem with the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub oaks are small shrubby oaks, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Revolutionary character signifying love is seen in market-place

indicators.note: these pieces are seen within the other, so they go inside

parts.note: a mart is a market
an X at the end of a letter stands for a kiss, a sign of love

explanation.surface: A rebel's letter of love appears in the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist follows the revolutionary communism of Karl Marx.

clue.text: Bird losing a bit of a foot in rubbish

indicators.note: the bird loses something, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the chaffinch is a common European finch
an inch is a twelfth of a foot

explanation.surface: A bird hurts its foot in a rubbish heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is husks separated from grain, hence worthless stuff or rubbish.

clue.text: Dissolute character with people at work by river

indicators.note: one piece set by (next to) the other, here following it

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a workforce is the staff

explanation.surface: A debauched figure is seen with the workforce beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Sir John Falstaff is the archetypal drunken, debauched rogue.

clue.text: Debasement of adult taking drug, fixed amount

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A grown-up degrades themselves by taking a set dose of a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulteration is the corruption of something pure by mixing in inferior matter, a lowering of quality.

clue.text: Little Mary's opening with style

definitions.note: Little Mary is old slang for the stomach, so this means of the stomach

parts.note: a stoma is a small opening, as in a leaf or the body
chic is stylishness

explanation.surface: A small girl named Mary begins her day with style.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Mary is a dated British euphemism for the stomach, from J M Barrie's play of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stomachic means relating to the stomach, the organ jokingly called Little Mary.

clue.text: Liar offering series of anecdotes, a sin confusing characters

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about someone

indicators.note: the letters are confused, mixed into another order

explanation.surface: A fibber tells a run of stories, jumbling the facts of his sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing characters' rearranges A SIN to make NIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Acts, Ananias lied to the apostles and was struck dead, so his name means a liar.

clue.text: Get ability to fly, initially from shelf of rocks

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow rocky shelf

explanation.surface: A young bird first learns to fly from a cliff ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird fledges when it grows the feathers needed for flight.

clue.text: Have another look at part of CH system before getting stuck in

indicators.note: one word is lodged inside the other, so its letters go into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: CH is central heating; a radiator, informally a rad, is part of it
ERE is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone checks again on a component of the heating before getting to work on it.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the usual British abbreviation for central heating, whose radiators are called rads.
explanation.definitionFit: To reread a text is to go over it a second time, another look at it.

clue.text: In France you may have to get angry in teacher's office

parts.note: TU is the familiar French word for you
to rage is to get furiously angry

explanation.surface: A French teacher may lose their temper in the staffroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorage is the post or function of a tutor, a teacher's role or office.

clue.text: A constraint's awkward for business deals

indicators.note: the letters are put in an awkward, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A restriction makes commercial agreements difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges the letters of A CONSTRAINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Commercial deals between parties are transactions, in the plural.

clue.text: Attend work to deal with computers? Expect trouble!

definitions.text: Attend work to deal with computers?
definitions.meaning: whimsically, to be present on duty for information technology work
the idiom for being certain to get a punishment or scolding

explanation.surface: Turning up at the office to fix the computers is asking for problems.
explanation.walkthrough: IT stands for information technology, so the phrase literally means being at work for computing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means one is going to be punished or face unpleasant consequences.

clue.text: Imitating a sound on the microwave?

parts.note: a microwave oven goes ping when it finishes

explanation.surface: Someone copies the chime a microwave oven makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, so the participle means copying.

clue.text: Athenian captured by lawless fellow who opposes the king?

indicators.note: the first-named is held captive inside the other, so its letters sit within the second piece

parts.note: an anarchist rejects all law and government
Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's misanthrope

explanation.surface: A man from Athens is seized by a lawless rebel set against the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon is the title character of Shakespeare's Timon of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A person against monarchy, a republican, opposes rule by a king or queen.

clue.text: Spooner's unsophisticated method that allows transmission of messages

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: coarse means crude, unrefined
a mode is a way or method

explanation.surface: A crude technique of the famously muddled clergyman lets people send signals.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of COARSE MODE gives the telegraph code of dots and dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code was devised for telegraphy, the sending of messages over wire or radio.

clue.text: Cunning bridge over loch

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: an arch is a bridge-like span
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A clever span crosses a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness, a Scottish lake, is shortened to its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Archness is slyness or playful knowingness, a kind of cunning.

clue.text: Too fussy about detail

parts.note: OVER can mean concerning or about
a particular is an individual item or detail

explanation.surface: Someone is excessively finicky about the small things.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively fastidious or exacting is what being far too fussy means.

clue.text: Virginia has visitor least inclined to get to the point

definitions.text: least inclined to get to the point

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia has a caller who rambles on endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The most vague person is the most imprecise, the one who most avoids being specific.

clue.text: Key support for entertaining a big noise

indicators.note: one piece entertains, holds as a guest, the others inside it

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: An important backer is hosting a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noise' suggests a VIP, but here it is a din.
explanation.definitionFit: Key and leading both mean principal or most important.

clue.text: Ground is good, thought highly of

parts.note: rated means esteemed, thought highly of

explanation.surface: A sports venue is decent and well regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a playing field but is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Grated and ground both describe food reduced to small particles by grinding or rubbing.

clue.text: Scoundrel in shoes worn away at the sides

indicators.note: the edges are worn off, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: brogues are sturdy decorated leather shoes

explanation.surface: A villain wears shoes whose edges have been scuffed through.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal or villain.

clue.text: Philosophical system is needed by every single PM

parts.note: the Tao is the Chinese philosophy of the Way
each means every single one

explanation.surface: A prime minister needs a way of thinking that every person can follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish head of government holds this title.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official title of the Prime Minister of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Organisation no longer bottom, given zero

parts.note: the seat is one's bottom
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A body that is no longer at the bottom of a league, having scored nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SEATO, the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization, was dissolved in 1977.
explanation.definitionFit: SEATO was a Cold War defence alliance, now defunct.

clue.text: In close combat using digital resources?

definitions.meaning: fighting face to face, at very short range
humorously, using the toes, which are digits

explanation.surface: A fight at close quarters is fought with technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but toes are digits.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes direct confrontation at very close range.

clue.text: Material in the morning brought in to where builders work?

indicators.note: one piece is carried into the other, so its letters go inside

parts.note: builders work on a building site
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Supplies are delivered to a construction site early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Samite is a heavy silk fabric, often interwoven with gold, worn in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: He's timid about believing in two gods

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A shy man hesitates about a double faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of HE'S TIMID.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditheism is the doctrine of two gods, typically opposed good and evil powers, so a belief in a pair.

clue.text: Opposing silly talk in dances

parts.note: CON, as in pros and cons, means against
gas is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the foolish chatter at the dances.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance, so the plural names several such.
